arxiv_metadata_candidate.abstract: QIK-VRT combines semantic problem solving with persistent, source-bound working memory, authorized action paths, and verifiable effect readback. Its design objective is to improve capabilities while preserving evidence, provenance, authorization, and completion boundaries. A conditional wrapper construction describes integration of heterogeneous systems under computable observation and action adapters and terminating acceptance checks; it guarantees neither arbitrary target reachability nor universal speedup. The paper distinguishes formal derivation, empirical evidence, documentary attribution, interpretation, normative requirements, and open claims. It preserves a frozen 3 October 2026 source report, including nine recalculated microbenchmark median pairs, a source-bound 1/2/4-process comparison, two isolated methodological controls, and an Authority/Mirror credential-delivery HOLD. These subjects do not establish distributed production speedup or new replication of historical timing trials. Self-continuity is a testable functional profile, while phenomenal experience, universal truthfulness enforcement, all-node product acceptance, and physical FPGA execution remain unestablished. Delivery windows are conditional engineering scenarios rather than promises. This complete English successor preserves all 30 claim dispositions and explicitly separates prior effect authorization from subsequent task acceptance. No claim is promoted to FORMAL_PROVED, and no destination submission or scientific consensus is claimed.
